question: An engineer is implementing NPV mode on a Cisco MDS 9000 Series Switch. Which action must be taken?
options: NPIV must be enabled on the upstream switch.
The FCNS database must be disabled in the fabric.
A port channel must be configured to the upstream switch.
All switches in the fabric must be Cisco MDS switches.
theory: NPV (N Port Virtualization) lets an edge switch relay FLOGIs from its connected hosts upstream instead of consuming its own domain ID; every one of those relayed logins arrives at the upstream 'core' switch over a single NP uplink and must be translated into multiple, independently addressable FCIDs on that link. That translation is exactly what NPIV (N Port ID Virtualization) provides, so the upstream/core switch must have NPIV enabled for an NPV edge switch to function correctly against it. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - NPIV and NPV)
